name: N Seoul Tower
shortDescription: Seoul's landmark tower on Namsan — the city's default first view, and its most photographed one after dark.

name: Lotte World Tower & Mall
shortDescription: Seoul's tallest building — a 555-meter Jamsil complex holding a mall, hotel, and cinema, with the Seoul Sky observatory as just one part of it.

name: Seoul Sky
shortDescription: The observation deck on floors 117–123 of Lotte World Tower — the highest vantage point in Seoul, with a glass floor underfoot.

name: Seoul City Wall
shortDescription: Hanyangdoseong, the 18.6-kilometer Joseon-era fortress wall that still traces four of Seoul's inner mountains — a walking route as much as a monument.

name: Jeongdong Observatory
shortDescription: A free public viewpoint on the 13th floor of Seoul City Hall's Seosomun annex, looking straight down over Deoksugung Palace.

name: Gimpo Int'l Airport Observatory Deck
shortDescription: An outdoor deck on the domestic terminal's 4th floor at Gimpo International Airport, close enough to watch aircraft taxi and take off.

name: Cultural Complex J-Bug
shortDescription: A caterpillar-shaped cultural complex inside Ttukseom Hangang Park — officially Seoul Saenggak-maru — with a library, café, and river-facing views.
serviceDetail: Riverside cultural complex — library, café & exhibits

name: 63 Skypicnic
shortDescription: A newly reopened art-and-media observatory on the 60th and 63rd floors of Yeouido's 63 Building.

name: Riverview 8th Avenue
address: 서울 강동구 선사로 4 광진교 중앙지점 하단
shortDescription: A glass-floored viewing platform built into a pier of Gwangjin Bridge — one of only three bridge-pier observatories in the world.

name: Chaeseokjang Observatory
shortDescription: A rooftop viewpoint built atop a former Japanese colonial-era quarry cliff in Changsin-dong, with a café built into the level below.

name: Eungbongsan Palgakjeong
shortDescription: A traditional octagonal pavilion at the summit of Eungbongsan — one of Seoul's classic Han River night-view spots, reached by a short hike.

name: Namdaemun Market
shortDescription: Korea's largest traditional market, next to Sungnyemun Gate — clothing, housewares, and ginseng across about 20,000 wholesale and retail shops.

name: Kwangjang Market
shortDescription: Korea's first permanent private market, opened in 1905 — a food alley of bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, and yukhoe, alongside a second-floor fabric wholesale trade.

name: Ssamzigil
shortDescription: A four-floor craft-shopping complex in Insadong, built around a spiral ramp that lets you walk the whole building without stairs.

name: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market
shortDescription: Seoul's largest wholesale fish market, run by Suhyup — buy from the tanks on the trading floor, then have it prepared at one of the restaurants upstairs.

name: Majang Meat Market
shortDescription: Korea's largest meat wholesale market, in Seongdong-gu — around 1,500 stalls trading hanwoo and other cuts, many of which will grill what you buy on the spot.

name: Jungbu Market
shortDescription: A wholesale dried-seafood market in Euljiro — laver, seaweed, anchovies, squid, and pollack, sold by the box and in smaller retail quantities.

name: Mangwon Market
shortDescription: A neighborhood market in Mapo-gu selling fruit, vegetables, seafood, and street-food snacks, close to both Mangnidan-gil and Hangang Park.

name: Garak Market
shortDescription: Korea's first public wholesale market for produce and seafood when it opened in 1985, and now the country's largest — fruit, vegetables, and fisheries products traded at wholesale in Songpa-gu.

name: Seoul Folk Flea Market
shortDescription: An indoor flea market in seven color-coded buildings in Dongdaemun-gu — antiques, secondhand clothing, and household curios across nearly 900 shops.

name: Dongmyo Flea Market
shortDescription: An open-air secondhand market along the stone walls of Dongmyo Park, where merchants have gathered since the 1980s — vintage clothing and shoes are its biggest category now.

name: Mapo Agricultural & Marine Products Market
shortDescription: A two-story seafood and produce market near Seoul World Cup Stadium — shops on the ground floor, sashimi centers and restaurants upstairs.

name: Gongdeok Market
shortDescription: A neighborhood market on Mallijae-ro in Mapo-gu, home to Jokbal Alley — a row of braised pig's-trotter restaurants — and, next to it, a Jeon Alley of Korean savory pancakes.

name: Jongno 3-ga Stalls Alley
shortDescription: A stretch of orange-tented pojangmacha food carts near Jongno 3-ga Station that sets up after dark — seafood, tteokbokki, and fried snacks eaten standing at plastic tables.

name: Yeongdeungpo Market
shortDescription: An old neighborhood market in Yeongdeungpo-gu, with a lane of sundae (blood sausage) shops facing each other from both sides.

name: Shinheung Market
shortDescription: A 1950s covered market in Haebangchon, at the foot of Namsan, now home to independent bookstores, vintage shops, and cafés under a new transparent roof.

name: Gongneungdong Goblin Market
shortDescription: A neighborhood market in Nowon-gu at the end of the Gyeongchun Line Forest Trail, tracing back to vendors who gathered by the old Gyeongchun railway line.

name: Yeongcheon Market
shortDescription: A covered market in Seodaemun-gu, by Dongnimmun (Independence Gate) — once one of Seoul's largest wholesale rice-cake markets.

name: Myeongdong Night Market
shortDescription: Myeongdong's nightly street-food corridor — stalls set up along Myeongdong-gil and its side streets each evening, running roughly from dusk to around midnight.

name: Starfield COEX Mall
shortDescription: The underground mall beneath the COEX complex in Samseong-dong, holding an aquarium, a multiplex and a free public library.

name: GOTO Mall
shortDescription: The 620-shop arcade under the Express Bus Terminal — the largest of the 25 underground arcades the city operates.

name: I'Park Mall
shortDescription: The eleven-floor mall built into Yongsan Station — department store halls, an electronics centre, a cinema and an e-sports arena.

name: Lotte Outlets Seoul Station
shortDescription: Three outlet floors inside the Seoul Station building, carrying 84 brands above a Lotte Mart.

name: IFC Mall
shortDescription: Three basement levels under the International Finance Centre towers on Yeouido, reached from the station by a 360-metre moving walkway.

name: Common Ground
shortDescription: A complex assembled from 200 shipping containers outside Konkuk University, open since April 2015.

name: Myeongdong Underground Shopping Center
shortDescription: A 61-shop arcade under Namdaemun-ro listed for eyewear and clothing — and entered from Euljiro 1-ga Station, not Myeongdong Station.

name: Apm Place
shortDescription: A twelve-storey wholesale fashion building in Dongdaemun that trades overnight, from 8pm to 5am, and closes at weekends.

name: Stylenanda Pink Hotel Flagship Store
shortDescription: Stylenanda's Myeongdong flagship — a store fitted out to look like a hotel, carrying the brand's 3CE cosmetics line.

name: Mecenatpolis Mall
shortDescription: An open-air street mall at the foot of the Mecenatpolis towers in Hapjeong, connected directly to the station.

name: Garden 5
shortDescription: A four-hall retail complex at Jangji Station, built by the city to rehouse traders displaced by the Cheonggyecheon restoration.

name: Nampyeonghwa Sangga
shortDescription: A wholesale market for bags and clothing on the Dongdaemun edge of Jung-gu, trading since 1980 across a basement and three floors.

name: Hello APM
shortDescription: A Dongdaemun fashion building that trades retail rather than wholesale, with the clothing on its lower four floors — open to 1am, closed Tuesdays.

name: Myeongdong Migliore
shortDescription: Two retail floors at Myeongdong Station Exit 6, under fifteen storeys of hotel — remodelled and reopened in August 2024.

name: Bukhansan National Park
shortDescription: A mountain national park easily accessible from central Seoul

name: Changdeokgung Palace
shortDescription: A UNESCO World Heritage palace; its rear garden requires reservation

name: Cheonggyecheon Stream
shortDescription: A restored urban stream walkway popular for evening lighting displays

name: Daerim Central Market
shortDescription: Market in Yeongdeungpo, Seoul.

name: Deoksugung Palace
shortDescription: A palace tied to the Korean Empire era, open for night viewing

name: Garosu-gil
shortDescription: A trendy street lined with cafes and boutique shops

name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
shortDescription: The main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty, popular for hanbok photo experiences

name: Ihwa-dong Mural Village
shortDescription: A hillside village known for its murals and street art

name: Insadong
shortDescription: A street lined with traditional crafts and antique shops

name: Jeongdong Theater
shortDescription: A theater specializing in traditional Korean performing arts

name: Jongmyo Shrine
shortDescription: A Confucian shrine for Joseon royalty, a UNESCO World Heritage site

name: Jongno Tower
shortDescription: Observatory and tower in Jongno, Seoul.

name: Korea Furniture Museum
shortDescription: A reservation-only museum of traditional Korean furniture and hanok architecture

name: Leeum Museum of Art
shortDescription: A private museum spanning traditional and contemporary Korean art

name: Lotte World
shortDescription: An indoor-outdoor amusement park with an ice rink

name: MMCA Seoul
shortDescription: Korea's leading national museum of modern and contemporary art

name: Myeongdong NANTA Theater
shortDescription: A dedicated theater for the non-verbal performance NANTA

name: Myeongdong Shopping Street
shortDescription: A bustling shopping street known for fashion, K-beauty and street food

name: Namsan Park
shortDescription: A downtown park leading up to N Seoul Tower, popular for walking

name: Namsangol Hanok Village
shortDescription: A recreated hanok village with five restored traditional houses

name: National Folk Museum of Korea
shortDescription: A free museum showcasing traditional Korean folk life

name: National Museum of Korea
shortDescription: Korea's largest national museum covering the country's full history, free admission

name: National Palace Museum of Korea
shortDescription: A museum dedicated to royal artifacts of the Joseon dynasty

name: Seodaemun Prison History Hall
shortDescription: A memorial hall documenting Korea's colonial-era prison history

name: Seoul Arts Center
shortDescription: Korea's largest complex for performing arts and exhibitions

name: Seoul Children's Grand Park
shortDescription: A free park featuring a zoo and amusement rides

name: Seoul Museum of Art
shortDescription: A city museum of contemporary art located near Deoksugung Palace

name: Seoul Museum of History
shortDescription: A free museum tracing Seoul's 600-year history

name: The War Memorial of Korea
shortDescription: One of Asia's largest war museums, free admission

name: Times Square Mall
shortDescription: A large complex mall with a cinema, bookstore and various shops
